messages:
Ana M: Quick thought — our current pin semantics are too binary (pinned vs unpinned). What if we introduce pin affinity levels (hot/warm/cold) encoded in rollout metadata to guide eviction and placement?

Tomas G: +1. hot = never evict unless explicit; warm = keep for a grace period; cold = eligible for immediate reclaim. That maps well to tenant intents (prod vs test).

Priya S: How would metadata look on the wire? We should keep proto additive and values stringified for backwards compat. Example fields: affinity, fingerprint, human_change_note, policy_profile.

Ana M: sketch: 
```
affinity: "warm"
fingerprint: "sha256:abcd..."
policy_profile: "default-permissive"
human_change_note: "tokenizer bump + minor vocab"
estimated_memory_delta: "+320MB"
```
(we'll send actual as strings in proto)

Tomas G: fingerprint is important. If fingerprint changes and affinity stays warm, runtime can diff and decide whether change is structural (tokenizer/vocab/model-arch) vs surface (perf tweak). We should add a simple change_type hint: binary = "tokenizer"|"weights"|"quant"|"config".

Priya S: tenants should be able to opt into strict policies: e.g., strict-tenants treat any fingerprint change as immediate unpin. Others accept warm->hot promotion if observed traffic calls new version. We'll need a per-tenant policy reference in the metadata or a lookup table.

Ana M: runtime algorithm proposal (pseudocode):
```
on_metadata_update(pin, new_meta):
  if new_meta.affinity == "hot":
    keep_pin()
  elif fingerprint_changed(pin.meta, new_meta):
    if tenant_policy(pin.tenant) == "strict":
      evict_immediately()
    else:
      mark_as_warm_with_deadline(now + default_warm_window)
  elif only_label_changes:
    extend_warm_deadline(default_label_window)
  else:
    normal_eviction_path()
```

ops-bot: FYI — added schema fields affinity, fingerprint, change_type, estimated_memory_delta to staging rollout proto. Additive change only.

Tomas G: memory is key. If estimated_memory_delta present and > threshold, scheduler should avoid promoting to hot until capacity checked. Also a cluster-wide pressure flag (ops reclaim) should downgrade warm->cold.

Priya S: observability hooks: emit "rollout_notice" events with change_type and fingerprint so Console can group related rollouts. Add a small sample note field so on-call can triage quickly. Example: 
`rollout_notice: { "fingerprint":"sha256:abcd","change_type":"quant","note":"switch to int8, expect 2-3% perf variance" }`

DevRel: suggest we show these signals in our public docs as recommended best-practices for model authors. Small notes on how to set affinity & change_type to avoid surprises for customers.

Ana M: open questions: 1) default warm window length, 2) how to compute fingerprint reliably (should include tokenizer & config), 3) how to surface estimated_memory_delta (best-effort from build).

Tomas G: propose defaults: warm_window = 24h, label_window = 4h, strict tenants opt-in flag in tenant profile. Fingerprint algorithm = sha256 over canonicalized {model-config, tokenizer-spec, vocab-hash}. Put exact spec in RFC.

Priya S: I'll draft RFC snippets and include examples of tenant policy YAML and runtime contract. Also include telemetry events names and sample Console cards.

Ana M: action items: Priya -> RFC + examples; Tomas -> fingerprint canonicalizer PR; DevRel -> docs snippet; Ops -> GC reclaim hook + pressure flag.

Tomas G: ack. small follow-up: consider an "auto-canary" mode — send a tiny fraction of traffic to new fingerprint while keeping warm pin, to detect regressions before full promotion. Could be in a separate follow-up RFC.

Ana M: love that. Ok that's it for now — next sync we'll review RFC draft. :sparkles:
